title: plugin-auth SCIM: provisioned accounts stay `source = env_native` ("Local Account"), so the managed-identity refusals never fire — the stamp waits for a `sys_account` insert that @better-auth/scim 1.7.x no longer makes
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, cloud `main` `de8d979` (framework pin `e24136c2`, `@better-auth/scim` 1.7.12), licensed, Postgres. Found during the local SCIM run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3667, using a SCIM 2.0 client that sends Okta's request shapes.

## What happens
1. Mint a SCIM credential (Setup → SCIM Credentials → Mint Credential) and send Okta's `POST /Users` (userName, name, emails, externalId, active). The answer is 201.
2. Setup → Users shows **Identity Source: Local Account** for the provisioned user. In the DB, `sys_user.source = 'env_native'`.
3. In `sys_account` the user has **no row at all**. The SCIM link lives in `sys_scim_user` / `sys_scim_subject`.

## Why
The only stamp on the SCIM path is the `afterInsert` hook on `sys_account` in `auth-plugin.ts` (the "Identity-source provenance for accounts created OUTSIDE better-auth's databaseHooks" block). Its comment says "@better-auth/scim creates `sys_account` at the adapter level". On 1.7.x it doesn't: the vendor now keeps its own tables (`sys_scim_user`, `sys_scim_subject`, tombstones) and never writes an account row. So the hook never fires, and no test pins a SCIM-created user reading `idp_provisioned`. The leaver e2e in cloud doesn't assert `source`.

## Consequences (measured unless marked)
- **Set Manager is accepted** on a SCIM user. `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager` returned 200 and wrote `manager_id`. Refusal 5 in `admin-set-user-manager.ts` ("the directory owns this identity") keys off `source === 'idp_provisioned'`. I cleared the value afterwards.
- **Setup → Users → row menu** offers Edit / Set Password / Set Manager for the SCIM user. **Set Password** worked from the UI: the user signed in with that password, then created API keys. On a cloud-managed environment, `admin/set-user-password` would also skip its `idp_provisioned` refusal (#25083), going by the code; not measured.
- **The user's own Profile page** lets them edit their Name. The directory overwrites it on the next push.
- The internal Okta/Entra setup docs in cloud (`docs/enterprise/scim-okta.md`) promise a provisioned account "has no password and signs in through SSO". Today that isn't true.

## Expected
Every user that a SCIM connection creates, or re-links through a tombstone, reads `source = 'idp_provisioned'`. Options:
- stamp from the SCIM create path itself, e.g. `identity.reconcileUser` / a hook on `sys_scim_subject`, instead of `sys_account`;
- or an `afterInsert` on `sys_scim_user`.

Backfill existing SCIM-linked users once at boot. Pin the fix with a test that goes through the real vendor `POST /Users`.

Related: #32087 item 5, which asks whether "Set Password" should be offered for IdP-provisioned users at all. That question only matters once SCIM users are actually marked.
